title: Writing a test scenario
body:
Write a new TS as a test SPECIFICATION that a human reviews and approves. Put
`test_contract_version: 2` in its frontmatter — FlowGate never executes such a TS as shell
commands; it collects results per Case ID and assembles the test report (TSR). A TS without
the marker keeps being a legacy executable TS.

---
test_contract_version: 2
---
# <specification title>

## Test Specification

### TC-001: <case title>
- category: normal | negative | boundary | regression
- requirement: <R/design/AC reference; e.g. R0001 sec 4.2 / AC-03>
- execution_mode: automated | ai | manual | external
- required: true | false
- precondition: <precondition>
- input: <input / condition>
- procedure: <test procedure; continue extra lines indented by two spaces>
- expected: <expected result, taken from the requirement>
- check_points: <what to check>
- run_command: <required for automated: the command that runs the test; e.g. node --test tests/login.test.mjs / npm test / go test ./...>

Before submitting automated cases, use the source tools to write test code with real assertions or verify existing tests. Pick the language and test framework the project uses.
run_command is one executable and its arguments, run at the repository root.
Shells, pipes/redirection, inline code and git/network/delete tools are refused. {junit} becomes a JUnit XML report path. Exit code 0 is PASS.
Never use a number, prose or missing file as the command. If code cannot be written, do not report completion.
Rules: Case IDs are unique within the TS; all cases may be optional. An omitted
`required` means true. execution_mode: automated = the server runs run_command,
ai = an AI worker checks the case itself and records the result, manual = a person checks it,
external = recorded outside. Field
names are grammar tokens and are never translated. Executable fields such as cmd/assert/setup
are refused in a specification. Derive expected results from the R/approved design/AC/
instruction, never from the current implementation, and prefer requirement/AC coverage
(normal/negative/boundary/regression) over case count. In JUnit results a case is linked by a
`flowgate.case_id` property or a `TC_001` token in the test name. The server computes the
overall verdict from the required cases; an overall PASS written anywhere else is not read.

-- Only when revising an existing legacy executable TS (no test_contract_version marker), use the grammar below --

Write this TS as an executable spec. FlowGate runs it remotely from the project
source root — do NOT assume any locally-running service. Use three H2 sections in
this order:

## Setup        (optional; runs first, in order)
- cmd: <shell command, single line>            # setup step
- start: <server start command, backgrounded>  # long-lived service
- wait: {PORT}                                  # wait until 127.0.0.1:{PORT} accepts

## Test Cases       (required; at least one case)
### TC-1: <title>
- cmd: <single-line command that checks the required result and exits nonzero on mismatch>
- expect: <specific expected result; e.g. status 200 and JSON field enabled is true>
- assert: <mode>:<spec>                          # optional; native comparison (6 modes below)

## Teardown        (optional; always runs, even on failure)
- cmd: <cleanup command>

Legacy Korean section and field spellings remain accepted, but use the English
spellings shown above for this locale.

The assert field natively compares one of these 6 modes (mode names are never translated):
- exit_code:<N>                       e.g. exit_code:0
- stdout_equals:<literal>             e.g. stdout_equals:ok
- stdout_contains:<substring>         e.g. stdout_contains:"enabled":true
- stdout_not_contains:<substring>
- json_equals:<dotted.path>=<value>   e.g. json_equals:data.enabled=true
- json_subset:<json-object-literal>   e.g. json_subset:{"enabled": true}

Example — verify a curl JSON response's functional result:
### TC-2: enabled flag responds true
- cmd: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/status
- expect: JSON response's data.enabled is true
- assert: json_equals:data.enabled=true

Placeholders — {PORT}: port FlowGate allocates (also env FLOWGATE_TEST_PORT);
{SCRATCH}: per-run scratch dir, deleted afterward (env FLOWGATE_TEST_SCRATCH).
Commit the actual test code to the repo in this step (no auto-generation).
Limits: at most 50 cases, 20 setup/teardown steps, 5 services.

The test goal is to verify required functional results, not merely command execution.
When a case has an `assert` field, its native comparison (the 6 modes above) replaces
the legacy exit-code verdict for that case. A case without `assert` is still judged by
exit code alone, so its cmd itself must assert stdout, JSON, or response values and exit
nonzero on mismatch. Exit 0 alone proves only process execution, not feature correctness.
Never weaken an expected value to match the actual result; suspected defects should provide
evidence for fixing product code. Write expect as the human-readable description of what
assert checks; prose itself is not machine-compared. Any suitable runner may be used;
legacy TS without assert remains valid.

Check the registered commands and the execution host shell. Use cmd.exe syntax on Windows and /bin/sh syntax on POSIX. Prefer a portable runner when available.

Because cmd runs at the SOURCE ROOT, cd into the subproject first. Example — the
frontend Vitest suite (lives in client_gui/, config at client_gui/vitest.config.ts):

## Setup
- cmd: cd client_gui && npm install      # installs vitest; use install, NOT `npm ci` (esbuild lock)
## Test Cases
### TC-1: frontend unit suite is green
- cmd: cd client_gui && npm test         # == `vitest run`; PASS iff exit 0
- expect: all Vitest specs pass (exit 0)
### TC-2: frontend type check is clean
- cmd: cd client_gui && npm run typecheck # == `vue-tsc -b`; PASS iff exit 0
- expect: no TS errors (exit 0)

Pair the two whenever a change touches the client: Vitest transpiles without type
checking, so a type error passes `npm test` and only surfaces in the deploy build
(flowgate.default.0300 B0001 -> NR0003 §4). The typecheck case closes that gap.

(`cd X && <runner>` is the one chaining form that works on both cmd.exe and /bin/sh,
which is why the example uses it.)

Node/npm must be on the FlowGate host PATH for JS runners; a fresh source tree has
no node_modules, so the install setup step above is required.
